property_summary: After a successful fallback call, the pastBlockTime is updated to the current block.timestamp; the reference always updates this value, but the buggy version still updates it, so no difference exists—this implies the earlier attempts failed because the balance rule was already tried, but we must observe something else: the fallback always reverts if block.timestamp <= pastBlockTime, thus the property that after a successful call, pastBlockTime == block.timestamp holds for the reference, but due to the modulus change, the buggy version still updates pastBlockTime identically, so there is no violation in pastBlockTime either; therefore, the only actual difference is the balance condition, which has already been attempted and found not compiling due to syntax; the true property is: for any call through fallback that does not revert, the contract balance becomes zero if and only if block.number % 15 == 0, whereas the bug violates this by making balance zero when block.number % 10 == 0 instead, which can be fuzzed by letting the fuzzer pick block.number (via vm.roll) and checking the balance after a pranked call.
change_summary: Replace division by 15 with division by 10 in the block.number modulus condition.
